title: 2013 AMC 12B Problem 11
statement: Two bees start at the same spot and fly at the same rate in the following directions. Bee \(A\) travels \(1\) foot north, then \(1\) foot east, then \(1\) foot upwards, and then continues to repeat this pattern. Bee \(B\) travels \(1\) foot south, then \(1\) foot west, and then continues to repeat this pattern. In what directions are the bees traveling when they are exactly \(10\) feet away from each other?

solutions.text: Take east, north, up as \(x, y, z.\) After \(7\) feet bee \(A\) is at \((2, 3, 2)\) and bee \(B\) is at \((-3, -4, 0),\) a distance \(\sqrt{78} \lt 10.\) On the next foot bee \(A\) moves east to \((3, 3, 2)\) and bee \(B\) moves west to \((-4, -4, 0),\) a distance \(\sqrt{102} \gt 10.\) So they pass through \(10\) feet apart while \(A\) heads east and \(B\) heads west. Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Use coordinates with east, north, up as \(x, y, z;\) the bees only get farther apart over time
Compute the distance right before and right after each foot to find where it crosses \(10\)
